Question_text: Desmond wants to be a successful entrepreneur. He has decided to leave his office job to start up a gardening business cutting grass and planting flowers. It will be an unincorporated business. Desmond is aware that a new business is at greater risk of failure than an established business. He has identified his business objectives for the first year. Desmond has calculated he will need $750 for his start-up capital.

Parts.part_text: Define 'unincorporated business'.
Identify two objectives a new business might have.
Identify four characteristics of a successful entrepreneur.
Explain two reasons (other than lack of finance) why Desmond's new business might be at greater risk of failure than an established business.
Do you think owner's savings are the most suitable source of finance for a start-up business? Justify your answer.

Question_text: LCT manufactures cooking pots. It has 16 employees. As a small business LCT uses social media as its method of advertising. The owner, Carole, knows having a good brand image is important. She is analysing LCT's break-even chart. This is shown in Fig. 2.1. Carole is considering possible ways to lower LCT's break-even level of output.
image: Fig. 2.1: A break-even chart for LCT. The x-axis is labeled 'units' ranging from 0 to 1000 in increments of 100. The y-axis is labeled 'costs/revenue ($)' ranging from 0 to 12000 in increments of 2000. Three lines are plotted: 'fixed costs' (a horizontal line at $2000), 'total costs' (a line starting at $2000 and increasing with units), and 'total revenue' (a line starting at $0 and increasing with units). The 'total costs' and 'total revenue' lines intersect at the break-even point, which appears to be at approximately 200 units and $4000.
Topic: 4.2 Costs, scale of production and break-even analysis

Parts.part_text: Identify two limitations of break-even analysis.
Calculate LCT's profit if it sells 800 units. Show your working.
Outline two possible benefits to LCT of having a good brand image.
Explain two ways LCT might lower its break-even level of output.
Do you think social media is the best method of advertising for a small business to use? Justify your answer.

Question_text: ACP manufactures computers. Being ethical is important to ACP. The business employs 3000 workers in its factory. ACP imports 65% of its raw materials. As internal users of accounts, the directors plan to analyse ACP's financial performance using profitability ratios. The Finance Director thinks making a profit is more important for a business than managing its cash flow.
Sub_topic: Ratios: gross profit margin, profit margin, return on capital employed, current ratio, acid test ratio

Parts.part_text: Identify two external users of accounts.
Identify two profitability ratios.
Outline two possible reasons why ACP imports its raw materials.
Explain one benefit and one limitation to ACP of being ethical.
Do you think making a profit is more important for a business than managing its cash flow? Justify your answer.

Question_text: MRN is a food retailer. It has 490 shops and 70000 employees. MRN has announced plans to close 80 of its shops. The Human Resources Director said: '20% of management jobs will be removed. We want to encourage delegation. MRN will continue to follow legal controls over employment.' MRN's directors know it is important that businesses respond to increased competition.
Sub_topic: Importance of delegation, trust vs control

Parts.part_text: Define 'delegation'.
Identify two legal controls over employment.
Outline two functions of MRN's shop managers.
Explain two factors MRN should consider when deciding which shops to close.
Explain two ways a retail business could respond to increased competition. Which would be the best way to use? Justify your answer.
